text:
meera: Customer on v2 API is getting intermittent parse failures when using JSON mode. They see valid JSON most of the time but ~15% of calls return "broken JSON" (trailing commas, lone commas, or an extra token).

alex: do we have a correlated deploy/time window? any model changes or rollout?

meera: reported after the 02:15 deploy yesterday. No model swap, just runtime patch. Logs show a few 502s and some streaming cutoffs.

ingrid: can you paste an exact raw response from the customer? we need the failure case to craft a repair prompt or regex.

meera: pasted below (sanitized):
```
{"items": [{"id": "a1", "val": 12},]
```

meera: note the trailing comma before the ] and occasionally an extra `.` at the end.

alex: ok that's classic streaming trailer truncation. two immediate mitigations: 1) server-side circuit breaker + retry with backoff, 2) a lightweight client-side "json-scrub" fallback that tries safe regex fixes then re-ask if still invalid.

meera: customer wants repro steps so they can implement client-side fallback. posting suggested sequence below.

meera: 1) call the API with same params, capture raw_stream
2) attempt JSON.parse(raw_stream)
3) if parse fails, run regex cleanup: `s/\,\s*\]/\]/g; s/\,\s*\}/\}/g; s/\.(\s*)$//`
4) try parse again
5) if still fails, re-ask the model with a small self-heal prompt: `Please output only valid JSON that conforms to schema X. If you truncate, finish the object.`
6) use exponential backoff when re-asking (500ms * 2^n, max 8s) and max 3 retries

ingrid: add a final safety: if re-ask returns non-json, return a structured error object to the app so it can render a helpful UX instead of crashing. e.g. `{ "error": "parse_failed", "attempts": 3 }`

ria-support: ops note — on server side we rolled out a streaming buffer change that could leave trailing commas when chunk boundary aligned with token separators. Eng-runtime already got pinged. Recommend enabling prefix caching to reduce chunk boundary variance as a short-term mitigation.

ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026 streaming-trailer-truncation. Priority P2. Assigned to eng-runtime.

alex: for the customer's repro script, here's a quick curl they can use to simulate truncation (pipe will cut last bytes):
```bash
curl -s -N "https://api.redwood.example/v2/generate" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"long output that will stream"}' | head -c -2 > truncated.json
python -c "import json,sys; print('ok' if json.loads(open('truncated.json').read()) else 'fail')" || echo 'parse fail'
```

meera: billing question from customer: are retries billable? they pinged because re-ask might double token costs.

billing-bot: per current policy, retries that are programmatic client-side are billed; we recommend using server-side heuristics (circuit-breaker + small re-asks limited to 3) and exposing metrics so customers can tune. Offer: provide a grace for first 24h after an acknowledged incident — contact acct exec for credit.

ingrid: follow-up: I'm pushing a small patch to the runtime to clamp the last chunk assembly to avoid leaving a trailing comma. will post PR and rollout ETA in 30m.

meera: passing this to customer with the regex + re-ask recipe and the repro curl. Also telling them about possible short grace on billing and the incident.

alex: long-term we should surface a "structured-output-mode" header that guarantees atomic JSON or returns a structured parse_error frame instead of free-form streaming. I'll draft RFC next week.

meera: thanks all. I'll update thread when customer confirms fixes or needs escalation to on-call. :thumbsup:
